stories.title: India’s economy projected to grow 7.1% in 2026‑27 as inflation rises
stories.summary: The RBI governor Sanjay Malhotra said the Indian economy is expected to grow 7.1 % in fiscal year 2026‑27, up from a prior estimate of 6.7 %. He warned that inflationary pressures are building and could affect the growth outlook. He described India’s resilience as remarkable despite turbulent global conditions.

stories.title: India aims to raise manufacturing share to 25% of GDP
stories.summary: India plans to increase manufacturing’s contribution from roughly 16% to 25% of GDP. In an Economic Times discussion, PwC India’s Vinod Kumar and JSW Group’s Srihari Kaninghat explained how AI is being used on the shop floor—particularly in steel production—to lower material costs and forecast equipment failures. They said AI could help make manufacturing more appealing to top engineering talent.
stories.why: Boosting manufacturing’s share is framed as a strategy to revitalize the sector and draw skilled engineers back from IT roles.

stories.title: Extent of rate hike cycle to depend on growth-inflation outlook: RBI Governor
stories.summary: Reserve Bank of India (RBI) Governor Sanjay Malhotra said the duration and extent of the rate hike cycle will be contingent on the actual growth-inflation developments and outlook. The governor and other five Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) members voted to raise the repo rate by 25 bps to 5.5 per cent.

stories.title: Australian MP Helen Haines loses both legs after car attack
stories.summary: Helen Haines, an independent member of the Australian parliament, was struck by a Toyota LandCruiser driven by 43‑year‑old Brendan Nugent outside her electorate office in Wangaratta. The incident, described by police as a deliberate attack, resulted in Haines losing both legs. Nugent was arrested shortly after the crash and faced multiple charges when he appeared in court on Wednesday.
stories.why: The case raises questions about the security of elected officials.
